response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_len, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS per_day FROM film GROUP BY rating), m AS (SELECT AVG(per_day) AS mean_pd FROM r) SELECT AVG(r.avg_len) AS avg_length, AVG(r.per_day) AS avg_per_day_rate, AVG(r.per_day - m.mean_pd) AS avg_excess FROM r CROSS JOIN m WHERE r.per_day > m.mean_pd

assumptions.assumption: A rating's per-day rate is the average over its films of rental_rate / rental_duration. The film-level ratio is computed first, then averaged.
The 'ignoring films with no length' condition only affects average length, because AVG skips NULLs. Per-day rate uses all films in the rating.
The final row averages the selected ratings' own averages, so each rating counts once. It does not pool films across the ratings.

alternatives.interpretation: A rating's per-day rate is its average rental_rate divided by its average rental_duration, instead of the average of per-film ratios.
